key_insight: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning (SPFT) uses a frozen initial model given privileged information to emphasize training tokens that better predict the correct outcome.
engineering_relevance: SPFT offers a token-weighted alternative to standard supervised fine-tuning for improving mathematical reasoning and code generation.
method: Analyze the target distributions induced by dynamic and static token-weighting objectives.
Use a frozen initial model conditioned on privileged information, such as ground truth, to supply token-level weights.
Interpret the weighting through a Bayesian decomposition that favors tokens informative about the ground-truth outcome.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over standard SFT and other baselines across the main mathematical reasoning and code generation settings, without providing numerical results.
watch_item: Effectiveness depends on the quality of the frozen privileged prior, and computing its token-level guidance adds training-pipeline overhead.
